problems.title: Kernels of maximum-degree representations
problems.description: Can the largest irreducible representations collectively detect every element of a finite p-group?
problems.statement: Let G be a finite p-group, and let p^e be the largest degree of an irreducible complex representation of G. If p > e, must the intersection of the kernels of all irreducible representations of degree p^e be {1}?
problems.statement_latex: For a finite $p$-group $G$, set $p^e=\max_{\chi\in\operatorname{Irr}_{\mathbb C}(G)}\chi(1)$. Does $p>e$ imply $\bigcap_{\chi(1)=p^e}\ker\chi=\{1\}$?
details: The degree of a representation is its dimension. The question asks whether the representations of largest degree, taken together, distinguish every nonidentity group element.
The intersection ranges over every ordinary irreducible complex representation of that maximum degree.
scope: The integer e is the logarithm to base p of the largest character degree; it is not the exponent of G.
Collective faithfulness does not require a single faithful irreducible representation.
A proof for a restricted family of groups must retain that restriction.

problems.title: Simple twisted group algebras
problems.description: Must a finite group be soluble if one of its twisted group algebras over an arbitrary field is simple?
problems.statement: Let G be a finite group, let K be any field, and let α be a normalized 2-cocycle with values in K×. If the twisted group algebra K^α G is simple, must G be soluble?
problems.statement_latex: Let $G$ be a finite group, $K$ a field, and $\alpha:G\times G\to K^\times$ a normalized $2$-cocycle. If $K^\alpha G$ is simple, must $G$ be soluble?
details: The twisted group algebra has a K-basis indexed by G, with multiplication u_g u_h = α(g,h)u_gh. The cocycle identity ensures associativity.
Simple means that the algebra has no nonzero proper two-sided ideals. Its center is not required to equal K.

The AI generated manuscript proposes a full affirmative answer, covering characteristic zero and positive characteristic. It is available before human review, with its original verification notice intact.
scope: G is finite and K is arbitrary; no splitting-field or algebraic-closure assumption may be added.
Simplicity and central simplicity are distinct. The editors identify the central-simple case as known.
Soluble and solvable mean the same group-theoretic property.
A public proposed solution does not establish that the original problem has been settled.

problems.title: Augmentation ideals and the Jacobson radical
problems.attribution: I. Kaplansky · contributed by D. S. Passman
problems.description: When does the augmentation ideal of a group algebra coincide with its Jacobson radical?
problems.statement: For an arbitrary field K and a nontrivial group G, is J(K[G]) = I_K(G) equivalent to the existence of a prime p such that char K = p and G is a locally finite p-group?
problems.statement_latex: For a field $K$ and a nontrivial group $G$, is $J(K[G])=I_K(G)$ equivalent to $\operatorname{char}K=p>0$ and $G$ being a locally finite $p$-group?
details: The augmentation map sends a finite sum of group elements with coefficients in K to the sum of those coefficients. Its kernel is the augmentation ideal I_K(G).
The Jacobson radical is the intersection of the maximal right ideals. A group is locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup is finite.
scope: The group must be nontrivial; for the trivial group both ideals vanish in every characteristic.
K[G] denotes the ordinary group algebra, not a completion.
Elementwise p-power torsion alone does not assert local finiteness.

problems.title: Infinite groups of exponent five
problems.description: Can a finitely generated group be infinite if the fifth power of every element is the identity?
problems.statement: Does there exist an infinite finitely generated group G such that x^5 = 1 for every element x of G? Equivalently, is the free Burnside group B(d,5) infinite for some finite d ≥ 2?
problems.statement_latex: Does there exist a group $G=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_d\rangle$, for some finite $d\ge2$, such that $|G|=\infty$ and $x^5=1$ for every $x\in G$? Equivalently, is $B(d,5)$ infinite for some finite $d\ge2$?
details: Finite generation is essential: the question requires a fixed finite set of generators.
The identity must hold for every group element, including every word in the generators.
scope: This is part (b), which fixes exponent five.
The full Burnside group and the restricted Burnside group are different objects.
A negative answer must address every finite generating rank; checking rank two alone is insufficient.

problems.title: Minimum-rank overgroups in free groups
problems.description: Do the smallest-rank overgroups of a subgroup of a free group have a least and greatest member, with intersections and joins preserving that rank?
problems.statement: Let F be a subgroup of a free group H, and suppose F is contained in a finitely generated subgroup of H. Let r be the least finite rank of an overgroup of F in H. Must the rank-r overgroups have a greatest member and a least member, and be closed under subgroup joins and intersections? Neither F nor H is assumed finitely generated.
problems.statement_latex: For $F\le H$ with $H$ free and $F$ contained in a finite-rank subgroup, put $r=\min\{\operatorname{rk}(G):F\le G\le H,\ \operatorname{rk}(G)<\infty\}$. Does $\mathcal M=\{G:F\le G\le H,\ \operatorname{rk}(G)=r\}$ have a greatest and least member, and satisfy $A\cap B,\langle A,B\rangle\in\mathcal M$ whenever $A,B\in\mathcal M$?
details: The four parts concern a greatest member, closure under subgroup joins, a least member, and closure under pairwise intersections, respectively.
The proposed deduction answers all four affirmatively using existing results of Jaikin-Zapirain and Takahasi. It explicitly handles a possibly infinitely generated initial subgroup.
The November 2026 problem entry has no solution marker. The absence of a marker does not establish novelty; the deduction may already be known as a consequence of existing theorems.
scope: Neither the initial subgroup nor the ambient free group is assumed finitely generated.
Rank means the size of a free basis, with the trivial group of rank zero.
Join means the subgroup generated by the union, not a different closure operation.
The argument and AI review remain provisional; no human acceptance or established priority is claimed.

problems.title: Homomorphisms fixing a subgroup at a rank drop
problems.description: Does a minimal drop in subgroup rank force every homomorphism fixing the smaller subgroup to be inclusion?
problems.statement: Let K < H < F be free groups of finite rank. Suppose rank(H) < rank(K), and every proper subgroup L < H containing K has rank(L) >= rank(K). Must every homomorphism H -> F that fixes K pointwise be the inclusion?
problems.statement_latex: Let $K<H<F$ be free groups of finite rank, with $\operatorname{rk}(H)<\operatorname{rk}(K)$ and $\operatorname{rk}(L)\ge\operatorname{rk}(K)$ for every $K\le L<H$. Must every $\phi:H\to F$ with $\phi|_K=\operatorname{id}_K$ be inclusion?
details: The condition ranges over every proper intermediate subgroup, including those of infinite rank.
The proposed explicit counterexample has ranks 4, 3, and 2 for K, H, and F. A homomorphism fixes K but differs from inclusion.
The construction specializes an existing example of Lei and Zhang. A separate Schreier-graph argument checks the additional condition required by this question.
scope: Both subgroup inclusions are strict. Rank is free-basis rank, which need not increase under subgroup inclusion.
The alternative map has codomain F and need not take its values in H.
The November 2026 entry is unmarked. Novelty of this application has not been established; the underlying construction belongs to Lei and Zhang.
AI review is complete with no gap found; human acceptance and formal verification are not claimed.

preprints.title: Simple twisted group algebras over arbitrary fields
preprints.attribution_note: The mathematical argument and manuscript were generated by ChatGPT. The seminar has not yet reviewed this version. The supplied manuscript does not list human authors.
preprints.abstract: A proposed affirmative answer to Kourovka Problem 18.78 for arbitrary fields. The manuscript combines character-theoretic transitivity under group and Galois automorphisms, an affine reduction, and a characteristic-two argument. Galois descent and Witt-vector lifting connect the character theorem to simple twisted group algebras.
preprints.statement: For every finite group G, every field K, and every normalized 2-cocycle α: G × G → K×, simplicity of K^α G implies that G is soluble.

preprints.title: Minimum-rank overgroups of arbitrary subgroups of free groups
preprints.attribution_note: This manuscript and deduction were generated by ChatGPT/Codex. The essential external theorems are due to Jaikin-Zapirain and Takahasi. No human authorship, human acceptance, or established novelty is claimed.
preprints.abstract: An explicit deduction of affirmative answers to all four parts of Kourovka 20.11 from existing theorems. A Schreier-graph argument shows that intersecting all minimum-rank overgroups still gives an overgroup of that rank, even for an infinitely generated initial subgroup. Jaikin-Zapirain’s theorem then gives join closure, and Takahasi finiteness supplies the greatest overgroup. The family is a finite sublattice.
preprints.statement: If F is a subgroup of a free group H and is contained in a finite-rank subgroup, then its overgroups of minimum finite rank form a finite nonempty sublattice of the subgroup lattice of H, with least and greatest members.
preprints.review_summary: A separate Codex reviewer audited the full archived deduction on 6 November 2026 and found no mathematical gap, assuming the cited existing theorems. No repair was needed. Human review and novelty assessment remain pending; the deep external theorem was not independently re-proved.

preprints.title: A rank-drop counterexample to Kourovka Problem 20.8
preprints.attribution_note: This exposition and application were generated by ChatGPT/Codex. The underlying rank-three construction is due to Jialin Lei and Teng Zhang. No human authorship, human acceptance, or established novelty of the application is claimed.
preprints.abstract: An explicit negative answer to Kourovka 20.8. The example gives free groups K < H < F of ranks 4, 3, and 2, with every proper intermediate subgroup above K having rank at least four. A second homomorphism H -> F fixes K pointwise. The complete verification uses finite labelled graphs and word identities, with a separate AI audit and reproducible exact checks.
preprints.statement: There exist finite-rank free groups K < H < F with rank(H) < rank(K), such that every K <= L < H has rank(L) >= rank(K), but a homomorphism H -> F fixing K pointwise differs from inclusion.
preprints.review_summary: A separate Codex reviewer audited the complete archived candidate on 6 November 2026 and found no mathematical gap; no repair was needed. The audit checked all hypotheses, the universal intermediate-subgroup condition, and the homomorphism, and independently checked graph ranks. The review notes include the full verifier and its output. Human review and novelty assessment remain pending.
